title: Self-Evolving World Models for LLM Agent Planning
description: Research paper introducing self-evolving world models to improve LLM agent planning capabilities. The approach focuses on dynamic model adaptation for better agent performance in complex environments.
author: Xuan Zhang, Wenxuan Zhang, See-Kiong Ng, Yang Deng

title: Entity Binding Failures in Tool-Augmented Agents
description: Research analyzing entity binding failures in tool-augmented AI agents, addressing a critical challenge in agentic AI systems where agents struggle to correctly bind entities when using tools.
author: Rahul Suresh Babu, Shashank Indukuri

title: Whose Side Is Your Agent On? Multi-Party Principal Loyalty in LLM Agents
description: Research examining principal loyalty problems in LLM agents when multiple parties are involved, addressing alignment challenges in multi-agent systems.
author: Bojie Li, Noah Shi

title: MirrorCode: AI can rebuild entire programs from behavior alone
description: Research introducing MirrorCode, an AI system that can reconstruct entire programs by observing behavioral patterns alone, without access to source code. Represents significant advancement in program synthesis and reverse engineering.
author: Tom Adamczewski, David Owen, David Rein, Florian Brand, Giles Edkins, Allen Hart, Daniel O'Connell

title: Clarus: Coordinating Autonomous Research Agents toward Web-Scale Scientific Collaboration
description: Research presenting Clarus, a system for coordinating autonomous research agents to enable web-scale scientific collaboration. Addresses challenges in multi-agent coordination for complex research tasks.
author: Zihan Guo, Zeyi Chen, Zhiyu Chen, Zicai Cui, Shuai Shao, Bo Huang, Zhi Han, Yuanyi Song, Yuan Yuan, Chenxi Zeng, Xiaohang Nie, Zhengxi Yu, Hanwen Zhu, Junwei Liao, Ming Zhou, Yang Li, Yuanjian Zhou, Weinan Zhang

title: Dynamo: Dynamic Skill-Tool Evolution for Vision-Language Agents
description: Research introducing Dynamo, a training-free framework where frozen VLM agents evolve task-family-specific libraries of reasoning skills and executable visual tools. Addresses adaptation of Vision-Language Models to new visual reasoning tasks without retraining.
author: Yutao Sun, Yanting Miao, Hao-Xuan Ma, Mengyu Zhou, Mingshuai Chen, Tiancheng Zhao, Dexin Wang, Lei Lv, Li Xu, Xiaoxi Jiang, Guanjun Jiang

title: ManimAgent: Self-Evolving Multimodal Agents for Visual Education
description: Research presenting ManimAgent, self-evolving multimodal agents designed for visual education applications. The agents can adapt and improve their capabilities for educational content creation.
author: Wenjia Jiang, Zongyuan Cai, Yuanhang Shao, Chenru Wang, Boyan Han, Zhixue Song, Keyu Chen, Shengwei An, Xu Yang, Zhou Yang

title: State of AI in 2026: LLMs, Coding, Scaling Laws, China, Agents, GPUs, AGI
description: Lex Fridman Podcast #490 featuring Nathan Lambert and Sebastian Raschka discussing the comprehensive state of AI in 2026. Topics include Large Language Models, AI coding and programming, scaling laws, AI in China, AI Agents, GPUs and hardware, and AGI. A 4.5-hour deep dive into current AI progress and technical breakthroughs.
author: Lex Fridman with guests Nathan Lambert and Sebastian Raschka

title: Eight More Months of Agents: Learning to Supply LLMs with Context
description: Hacker News discussion about the evolution of AI coding agents over 8 months. Key insight: the skill is learning to supply LLMs with enough context to perform developer tasks like turning specs into code and checking work including generating tests.
author: Hacker News Community

title: Andrej Karpathy's 'Slopacolypse' Prediction and AI Coding Workflow Shift
description: Andrej Karpathy predicted 2026 would be the 'Slopacolypse' - a period where AI is suddenly writing most of his code. He reported experiencing 'atrophy' of his ability to write code manually due to heavy AI assistance, shifting from 80% manual+autocomplete coding and 20% agents to the reverse (80% agents, 20% manual) by February 2026.
author: Andrej Karpathy

title: Running Python Code in a Sandbox with MicroPython and WASM
description: Simon Willison details his latest sandbox experiment using MicroPython and WebAssembly to safely execute code. He created micropython-wasm, an alpha package for Datasette Agent that can generate and execute Python code safely. Notably, GPT-5.5 has so far failed to break out of the sandbox.
author: Simon Willison

title: OpenAI Launches Lockdown Mode to Prevent Data Exfiltration
description: Simon Willison analyzes OpenAI's new Lockdown Mode feature, designed to prevent the final stage of data exfiltration from prompt injection attacks by limiting outbound network requests. He explains how this directly attacks the 'exfiltration vectors' leg of the Lethal Trifecta (private data + untrusted content + data theft vectors).
author: Simon Willison

title: Uber Caps Usage of AI Tools Like Claude Code to Manage Costs
description: Simon Willison analyzes Uber's response to blowing their 2026 AI budget in four months by instituting a $1,500 monthly limit per AI coding tool per employee. The analysis reveals that Uber's AI spending cap is ~11% of median software engineer compensation ($330,000), suggesting a rational approach to managing agentic coding costs.
author: Simon Willison
